methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Infrastructure costs externalized onto residents signal that AI capability concentration in NoVA data centers creates public burden without distributing benefits, reinforcing metro-concentrated development patterns that deepen regional inequality.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free grassroots AI workshops led by a Norfolk native explicitly targeting the technology gap represents peer-to-peer knowledge distribution effort that could build deep, distributed capability outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership aims to distribute AI education beyond elite institutions through community impact focus, potentially creating secondary hub with genuine depth rather than just platform-level adoption.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College launching WorkAI Lab in traditionally underserved region signals institutional commitment to building deep AI leadership capacity outside NoVA-Richmond corridor, testing whether rural areas can develop expertise versus mere tool consumption.

signals.title: Virginia Tech secures $20m NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor lab - Cleanroom Technology
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's $20M NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor lab concentrates advanced technical capability in New River Valley, creating potential secondary excellence pocket but requiring intentional distribution mechanisms to avoid replicating NoVA concentration patterns.
